auditor: muse-spark-1.3 (Meta Model API), one call per section, reasoning_effort low
scope: compiled facts vs the handbook pages they cite (card backs are byte copies of these facts); exam items and lesson narration not checked in this pass

flagged.issue: Page states the permit supervision rule but does not state that a licensed driver may drive alone.
flagged.suggested_fix: The permit holder must be accompanied by a person licensed for that vehicle seated beside the permit holder.

flagged.issue: Page 12 alone does not list commercial Class A, B and C to show the letters are shared.
flagged.suggested_fix: North Carolina has a regular driver license and a commercial driver license, and most drivers need only Regular Class C.

flagged.issue: The page states the one-passenger rule but also allows a second under-21 non-household passenger for school trips and a household exception.
flagged.suggested_fix: When driving unsupervised there may be one under-21 non-household passenger, plus one other such passenger if a student driven directly to or from school, unless all passengers are household members.

flagged.issue: The page limits the mixed household/non-household ban to when driving unsupervised, which the fact omits.
flagged.suggested_fix: There is no under-21 limit if all passengers are household members; when driving unsupervised, under-21 household members may not be in the vehicle with under-21 non-household members.

flagged.issue: Page 15 states unsupervised driving is allowed but does not state on that page that Level Two is the first such level.
flagged.suggested_fix: Level Two allows driving without supervision from 5 a.m. until 9 p.m. and at any time when driving directly to or from work or a volunteer emergency service if a member.

flagged.issue: Page 15 states the six-month Level Two hold but does not state the nine-month Level One period for comparison.
flagged.suggested_fix: Level Two must be held at least six months before applying for a Full Provisional License.

flagged.issue: The page states the school-discipline triggers but does not state that traffic violations are excluded.
flagged.suggested_fix: License loss occurs if a student receives suspension for more than 10 consecutive days or alternative educational assignment due to discipline for more than 10 consecutive days.

flagged.issue: The page states driving outside a restriction counts as driving without a license but does not characterize it as not a minor infraction.
flagged.suggested_fix: If your license is restricted, you must only drive within the limits of the restriction; otherwise you are considered to be driving without a license.

flagged.issue: The statement omits the additional mail-renewal requirement for Social Security number/legal presence shown on the page.
flagged.suggested_fix: Add that NCDMV must have a record of Social Security number or U.S. government legal presence document.

flagged.issue: Page 28 states the five-year photo rule but does not state the eight-year military photo rule.
flagged.suggested_fix: Cite page 29 for the military eight-year photo rule, or limit the statement to the five-year civilian rule on page 28.

flagged.issue: Page 30 states the age-based durations but does not mention the knowledge test date.
flagged.suggested_fix: State only that license duration depends on age at issuance: 8 years for 18-65 and 5 years for 66 and older.

flagged.issue: Page 35 states the under-21 any-amount rule but does not state the adult per se comparison on that page.
flagged.suggested_fix: A driver under 21 convicted of driving with any amount of alcohol or drugs in their body has their license revoked for one year.

flagged.issue: Page 36 states reinstatement does not pertain to insurance points but does not state insurers use their own point system.
flagged.suggested_fix: Reinstatement cancels all previous driver license points, which does not pertain to insurance points.

flagged.issue: Page 55 states the farther-ahead and two-second-rule requirements but does not state on that page that stopping distance grows with speed.
flagged.suggested_fix: On page 55, allow safe distance under the two-second rule and see farther ahead as speed rises to allow enough distance for stopping.

flagged.issue: Omits the page's condition that moving right is required if the passing driver blows the horn.
flagged.suggested_fix: When being passed, help the other driver: if they blow the horn move to the right edge, and never increase speed.

flagged.issue: Page 65 states the crash risk but not the because-clause about riding to the right, which is on the prior page.
flagged.suggested_fix: A cyclist going straight through an intersection is at risk from a motorist turning right.

flagged.issue: The cited page states signs are divided into three types but only names Regulatory Signs on that page.
flagged.suggested_fix: Shape and color let you identify highway signs at a glance, and traffic signs are divided into three types, including Regulatory Signs.

flagged.issue: The cited page supports the pentagon school-zone part but does not mention the stop octagon or yield triangle shapes.
flagged.suggested_fix: The five-sided pentagon sign warns of a school zone or a school crossing.

flagged.issue: Cited page states the pedestrian left-side rule but does not state the bicyclist ride-with-traffic rule.
flagged.suggested_fix: Pedestrians should walk on the left side of the road facing traffic.
